First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-\frac{12}{\sqrt{y}}-2y\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-12{y}^{-1/2}-2y\cdot {y}^{1/2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(-12{y}^{-1/2}-2{y}^{3/2}) \\  & =-12\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/2})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2}) \\  & =-12(-\frac{1}{2}){y}^{-3/2}-2\cdot \frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2} \\  & =6{y}^{-3/2}-3{y}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{6}{y\sqrt{y}}-3\sqrt{y} \\  & =\frac{6-3{y}^{2}}{y\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{y\sqrt{y}}{6-3{y}^{2}}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(-14,1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-14,1)} & =\frac{1\sqrt{1}}{6-3(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
